questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go far away to explore a culture different from the one at home and it’s academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Most information came with Sydney Uni mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exchange coordinator Jane helped a lot and we had a meeting with the head of the bachelor’s programme at USYD Pharmacy School.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We had a bit of a mess getting a research project but the people at USYD were very helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy as I did it through USYD.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its completely fine! Sydney is a big city and it is nice to explore different areas. USYD is easily accessible with public transportation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very expensive. Queen Mary Building (cheapest one) has limited spots and sold out very fast.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was messy finding relevant courses and the lists provided was not helpful or adequate.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Search for courses and apply for multiple relevant courses to be approved. Choose from the approved courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could mail our USYD exchange coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Search courses online and not from the lists provided (they are not helpful..). Search approval for around 4 courses besides the bachelor’s thesis.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The overall academic level seemed a bit lower than at UCPH.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easier than courses from home. Bigger workload throughout the semester as assessments during semester counts in final score of the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Ongoing assessment during the semester is different. Same kind of lectures and tutorials (holdundervisning). All lectures are recorded. They take attendance (at least they can do).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Learning in Outdoor Education
Drug Design & Development
Research Methods (only to allocate points for the research project/bachelor’s thesis)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Do Learning in Outdoor Education if possible. Nice and easy and a good opportunity to meet other exchange students. 
Drug Design & Development was fairly easy and summed up different stuff from the bachelor programme from home and at the same time added new stuff.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Activities and travels is a big expense.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Get a concession (student prices) Opal Card to get half price of public transportation. 
Eating out is kinda cheap and buying coffee is very cheap compared to home. Groceries are a bit expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many different clubs. Many sports clubs are for advanced participants and not beginners.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many. I did boxing club, surfing society and underwater society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely do the surf camp with the surf society. But be sure to be ready to get tickets they sell out in a few minutes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel Australia!! I did Uluru, Tasmania, Cairns, Brisbane and Noosa. Also go to New Zealand, its so close and very beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Aussie life is pretty similar to Denmark but a bit more relaxed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to someone, they love to meet international people!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is so friendly and openminded.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not buy OSHC though uni, it is expensive. 
Be ready when accommodation is released, the cheapest ones sell out fast. 
Join some clubs to meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Australia is the best! Make sure to save a lot to travels while you are abroad.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Establishing a life in a new place and making so many new friends. 
Exchange life is very spontaneous and everyone is so committed to explore things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling alone before establishing friends and rutines.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is gonna be amazing!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
